data.title: Erythema nodosum — viva
data.summary: Reactive & drug eruptions · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Erythema nodosum** (Reactive & drug eruptions)_

**Q1. Define erythema nodosum (EN).**
- Commonest panniculitis — acute, tender, red, warm subcutaneous nodules mainly on shins, a delayed hypersensitivity reaction to various antigens; resolves without ulceration or scarring

**Q2. Causes (mnemonic: NODOSUM).**
- Idiopathic (30–50%)
- Infections: streptococcal pharyngitis (commonest in children), tuberculosis (important in India), Yersinia, Salmonella, Campylobacter, Chlamydia, Mycoplasma, histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, hepatitis B/C, EBV, leprosy (ENL is different), COVID-19
- Drugs: oral contraceptives/oestrogens, sulphonamides, penicillin, bromides, isotretinoin, vemurafenib/BRAF inhibitors
- Systemic disease: sarcoidosis (Löfgren syndrome), inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's > UC), Behçet's
- Pregnancy, malignancy (lymphoma, leukaemia)

**Q3. Describe the clinical features.**
- Young women 20–40 y (F:M ~5:1); prodrome of fever, malaise, arthralgia
- Bilateral, symmetrical, tender, bright red, poorly defined nodules 1–5 cm on anterior shins, also knees, ankles, thighs, forearms
- Evolve like a bruise (contusiform): red → purple → yellow-green (erythema contusiformis) over 2 weeks; never ulcerate; crops for 3–6 weeks

**Q4. What is Löfgren syndrome?**
- Acute sarcoidosis: EN + bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy + fever + migratory polyarthritis/periarticular ankle inflammation ± anterior uveitis; HLA-DRB1*03; excellent prognosis (spontaneous remission)

**Q5. Histopathology.**
- Septal panniculitis without vasculitis — thickened oedematous septa with lymphocytes, neutrophils (early), histiocytes
- Miescher's radial granulomas (small histiocytes around a central stellate cleft) — hallmark
- Deep incisional biopsy needed (punch may miss fat)

**Q6. Investigations to find the cause.**
- CBC, ESR/CRP, throat swab, ASO/anti-DNase B, Mantoux/IGRA, chest X-ray (TB, sarcoid hilar nodes), stool culture if diarrhoea, pregnancy test, serum ACE, IBD work-up (faecal calprotectin) if bowel symptoms, HBV/HCV

**Q7. Differential diagnosis.**
- Erythema induratum/nodular vasculitis (calves, ulcerate, lobular panniculitis with vasculitis)
- ENL in leprosy (anywhere, evanescent, systemic signs, smear positive)
- Cellulitis (unilateral), superficial thrombophlebitis, cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (livedo, nodules along vessels), lupus panniculitis, pancreatic panniculitis (ulcerate, oily discharge), α1-antitrypsin panniculitis, Sweet syndrome, subcutaneous lymphoma, insect bites

**Q8. Treatment.**
- Treat the underlying cause; stop OCP/drug
- Bed rest, leg elevation, compression, NSAIDs (indomethacin, naproxen, ibuprofen)
- Potassium iodide 300–900 mg/day (SSKI) for 3–4 weeks — useful in persistent cases (avoid in pregnancy/thyroid disease)
- Colchicine, hydroxychloroquine, dapsone; systemic steroids only after excluding infection (TB) and when severe
- EN in IBD — treat the bowel disease

**Q9. Differentiate septal from lobular panniculitis with examples.**
- Septal without vasculitis: EN, necrobiosis lipoidica, morphoea/scleroderma; septal with vasculitis: superficial thrombophlebitis, cutaneous PAN
- Lobular without vasculitis: lupus panniculitis, pancreatic, α1-antitrypsin, cold, factitial, sclerema/subcutaneous fat necrosis of newborn, lipodermatosclerosis; lobular with vasculitis: erythema induratum (nodular vasculitis), ENL

**Q10. Prognosis?**
- Self-limited in 3–6 weeks; may recur (with recurrent streptococcal infection or persistent cause); chronic/migratory variants rare

## Quick spotter facts
- Bilateral tender bruise-like shin nodules in a young woman — EN (never ulcerates)
- Miescher's radial granulomas
- EN + hilar nodes + arthritis — Löfgren syndrome

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Panniculitis). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
